oracle_provenance: Standard, foundational data-converter quantization-noise theory; independently hand-verified before implementation against the commonly cited ~98 dB (16-bit) and ~146 dB (24-bit) reference figures. Not copied from any shared Skill fixture.
scope: Bounded ideal ADC quantization SNR/ENOB check; not a noise-shaping/oversampling-aware model.

cases.question: Does a claimed 95 dB SINAD for a 16-bit converter sit below its 98.08 dB ideal quantization limit, as physically required?
For a 24-bit converter, does the ideal SNR limit match the commonly cited ~146 dB theoretical maximum?
Must a non-positive bit depth be rejected rather than producing a meaningless SNR limit?
When a claimed SINAD for a 16-bit converter exceeds its own ideal quantization limit, is that flagged as physically impossible rather than an exceptionally clean converter?
